newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-HEALY BOOSTS AUSTRALIA WITH RAPID 63.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HEALY BOOSTS AUSTRALIA WITH RAPID 63.

text.p: Ian Healy hammered 63 from 78 deliveries to give Australia a timely boost on the fourth morning of the fifth Ashes test against England at Trent Bridge on Sunday.
Wicketkeeper Healy responded positively after the touring team lost overnight batsman Steve Waugh for 14 to the second ball of the day.
Waugh drove Andy Caddick's opening delivery for four but the paceman snared him with the second, the batsman gloving a lifting delivery to Adam Hollioake at second slip.
However, Healy and Ricky Ponting, with an unbeaten 41, lifted Australia's second innings to 278 for six at lunch, when they led by 392.
Healy, cutting, driving and hitting effectively on the leg side, put on 105 in 104 minutes with Ponting for the seventh wicket, the Australian wicketkeeper completing his half-century in 49 balls.
Caddick was hit for 42 in six overs, and although off-spinner Robert Croft and Adam Hollioake staunched the flow a little, the 100 partnership still came up in 20 overs.
Healy had hit nine fours when he became Adam Hollioake's first wicket in test cricket when he edged one low to wicketkeeper Alec Stewart.
Australia, who lead the six-test series 2-1, need only draw here to retain the Ashes.
